chiripa-culture.name: Chiripa
chiripa-culture.summary: An archaeological culture that existed along the southern shore of Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, from about 1400 to 100 BCE.

chav-n-culture.name: Chavín culture
chav-n-culture.summary: A pre-Columbian civilization in Peru's northern Andean highlands, flourishing roughly 900 to 250 BCE, marked by an intensified religious cult and advances in ceramics, agriculture, metallurgy and textiles.

nazca-culture.name: Nazca culture
nazca-culture.summary: An archaeological culture that flourished from about 100 BC to 800 AD on Peru's southern coast, known for ceramics, textiles, geoglyphs, and underground aqueducts called puquios.

chav-n-de-hu-ntar.name: Chavín de Huántar
chav-n-de-hu-ntar.summary: An archaeological site in Peru with ruins dating back to as early as 1200 BC, serving as a major ceremonial center of the Chavín culture and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

cahuachi.name: Cahuachi
cahuachi.summary: A major ceremonial center of the Nazca culture in coastal Peru, active from about 1 to 500 CE and thought to have been a pilgrimage site rather than a capital.

three-sisters-agriculture.name: Three Sisters
three-sisters-agriculture.summary: A companion-planting method combining maize, beans and squash, in which each crop supports the others, developed by Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

paracas-culture.name: Paracas culture
paracas-culture.summary: An Andean society that existed roughly 800 to 100 BCE on Peru's south coast, known for irrigation skills and elaborate textiles; its Cavernas and Necropolis burial sites yielded richly decorated ceramics and cloth.

moche-culture.name: Moche culture
moche-culture.summary: A civilization that flourished in northern Peru from about 100 to 800 CE, likely a group of autonomous polities sharing culture rather than a single empire, known for rich art and architecture.

moche-valley.name: Moche Valley
moche-valley.summary: A fertile valley in northern Peru around the Moche River, farmed since pre-Columbian times and now home to the city of Trujillo.

neltuma-pallida.name: Neltuma pallida
neltuma-pallida.summary: A thorny mesquite tree native to coastal Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, known as huarango or kiawe, valued for preventing river and wind erosion.

raimondi-stele.name: Raimondi Stele
raimondi-stele.summary: A sacred carved granite stele of the Chavín culture (c. 1500–300 BCE) in Peru's central Andes, depicting the Staff God, now held in a Lima museum.

lanz-n.name: Lanzón
lanz-n.summary: A granite stela in the Old Temple of Chavín de Huántar in Peru's central highlands, erected around 500 BCE and likely linked to agrarian worship.

tello-obelisk.name: Tello Obelisk
tello-obelisk.summary: A carved granite monument of Peru's Chavín culture, found at Chavín de Huántar and named after the archaeologist who investigated it, Julio C. Tello.

tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
tiwanaku.summary: A major pre-Columbian archaeological site in Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, home to an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 people around 800 CE, with monumental structures and megalithic stonework.

staff-god.name: Staff God
staff-god.summary: A recurring front-facing figure holding an object in each hand, a religious icon shared across pre-Columbian Peru, with its oldest known depiction dated to 2250 BCE.

huaca.name: Huaca
huaca.summary: In Quechuan languages, an object or place considered sacred, often a monument or natural feature believed to hold spirits.

julio-c-tello.name: Julio C. Tello
julio-c-tello.summary: Peruvian archaeologist, 1880 to 1947, called the 'father of Peruvian archaeology' for discovering the Paracas culture and investigating Chavín de Huántar.

chakana.name: Chakana
chakana.summary: A stepped-cross symbol used by the Inca and earlier Andean societies for some 4,000 years, appearing in Chavín, Wari, Chancay and Tiwanaku art; its name means 'bridge' in Quechua.

akapana.name: Akapana
akapana.summary: An artificial earthen platform mound at the Tiwanaku site in Bolivia, shaped like a half Andean cross, 257 meters wide and 16.5 meters tall, faced with stone blocks including carved puma and human heads.

recuay-culture.name: Recuay culture
recuay-culture.summary: A pre-Columbian culture of highland Peru that flourished from about 200 BCE to 600 CE, related to the coastal Moche culture and named after Peru's Recuay Province.

lady-of-cao.name: Lady of Cao
lady-of-cao.summary: Name given to a female Moche mummy discovered at the El Brujo archaeological site, about 45 km north of Trujillo in Peru's La Libertad Region.

el-brujo.name: El Brujo
el-brujo.summary: An archaeological complex in Peru's Chicama Valley occupied since preceramic times, with its largest structures built later by the Moche culture.

trujillo-peru.name: Trujillo, Peru
trujillo-peru.summary: A city on Peru's northwestern coast, site of the earlier Moche and Chimú cultures, later declared the provisional capital of Peru by Bolívar in 1824.

paracas-textile.name: Paracas Textile
paracas-textile.summary: A mummy-wrapping textile from a 1920s-excavated necropolis in Peru, made by the Paracas culture around 200 to 300 BCE and embroidered with figures including flying shamans holding severed heads.

bernab-cobo.name: Bernabé Cobo
bernab-cobo.summary: A Spanish Jesuit missionary and writer (1582–1657) who spent 61 years in Spanish America and helped bring cinchona bark, source of quinine, to Europe.

aymara-language.name: Aymara language
aymara-language.summary: An indigenous language of the Bolivian Andes with over a million speakers, an official language of Bolivia and Peru alongside Spanish and Quechua.

quipu.name: Quipu
quipu.summary: Knotted-cord record-keeping devices used by Andean cultures, especially the Inca, to store numbers and other data in a decimal positional system; they date back to at least the 1st millennium CE.

proto-quechuan-language.name: Proto-Quechuan language
proto-quechuan-language.summary: The hypothetical ancestral language of the Quechuan language family, reconstructed from evidence in modern Quechua languages and ancient records.

puquina-language.name: Puquina language
puquina-language.summary: An extinct language once spoken around Lake Titicaca in Peru and Bolivia, associated with the Tiwanaku culture and still an official language of Bolivia, known mainly from a single 1607 document.

pedro-cieza-de-le-n.name: Pedro Cieza de León
pedro-cieza-de-le-n.summary: Spanish conquistador and chronicler (c. 1518–1554) whose Crónicas del Perú is considered fundamental to understanding Inca history and the empire's structure.

nazca-lines.name: Nazca lines
nazca-lines.summary: A vast group of geoglyphs made in the desert soil of southern Peru between 500 BC and 500 AD, covering about 50 square kilometers with straight lines and animal and plant figures.

paul-kosok.name: Paul Kosok
paul-kosok.summary: American professor of history and government credited as the first serious researcher of Peru's Nazca Lines, which he began studying in 1939 during field work on ancient irrigation systems.

maria-reiche.name: Maria Reiche
maria-reiche.summary: German-born Peruvian mathematician and archaeologist known as the 'Lady of the Lines' for documenting, preserving and publicising the Nazca Lines from 1941 until her death in 1998.

kotosh.name: Kotosh
kotosh.summary: Archaeological site near Huánuco, Peru, with a sequence of buildings spanning six periods of continuous occupation.

nicola-masini.name: Nicola Masini
nicola-masini.summary: Italian scientist (born 1965) known for studying traces of Andean civilizations in Peru and Bolivia using remote sensing technology.

giuseppe-orefici.name: Giuseppe Orefici
giuseppe-orefici.summary: An Italian archaeologist (1946–2025) known for his studies of the pre-Hispanic Nazca and Rapa Nui cultures.

san-pedro-cactus.name: San Pedro cactus
san-pedro-cactus.summary: A cactus, particularly the species Echinopsis pachanoi, that can contain the hallucinogen mescaline.

brooklyn-museum.name: Brooklyn Museum
brooklyn-museum.summary: Art museum in Brooklyn, New York City's second largest, holding around 500,000 objects including a major collection of Egyptian antiquities.

department-of-ica.name: Ica
department-of-ica.summary: A department of Peru on the Pacific coast, bordering Lima, Huancavelica, Ayacucho and Arequipa, with its capital at the city of Ica.

puquios.name: Puquios
puquios.summary: Ancient underground aqueducts that carry water long distances without evaporation loss in the dry coastal deserts of southern Peru and northern Chile, dozens of which still function today.

wari-kayan.name: Wari Kayan
wari-kayan.summary: An archaeological site on Peru's Paracas Peninsula, known for its ancient cemetery, the Paracas Necropolis, containing hundreds of well-preserved funerary bundles from the Paracas culture.
